Reviewed the diff against the post-change files and the `db.py` schema notes. Findings written to `findings.md`:

- `src/sync.py:14` — pagination drops the remainder page (`//` truncation), so e.g. 150 staged rows fetch only 100.
- `src/sync.py:24` — mutable default `seen=[]` makes the dedupe set global across calls; later syncs skip previously-seen users.
- `src/sync.py:35` — f-string SQL interpolation (injection + breakage on quotes); parameters were dropped.
- `src/sync.py:39` — `except: pass` replaces the previous `log.exception`, silently hiding all failures.
- `src/sync.py:31` — id added to `seen` before the UPDATE runs, so a failed row is skipped forever on retry.
- `src/report.py:7` — early return on empty `users` leaks the opened file handle and leaves an empty report (previously the header was written).
- `src/report.py:11` — `user["email"]` assumed non-None; schema says email is nullable, so this crashes (also `IndexError` on missing "@").
